finding: A cleanup exception could escape a discarded internal stage promise after output had already resolved, skipping active-count decrement and job removal and stranding queued work.
negativeControl: New failure test on the baseline resolved rather than rejected and produced an unhandled cleanup rejection.
contract: Publish output only after successful scope, cancellation-guard and transferred-input cleanup.
Attempt all cleanup, remove job slots and advance the queue on error. Discard failed output before admitting queued work.
Defer reentrant queue draining through settlement; preserve FIFO admission and one outstanding stage per job.
Cancellation wins as LAKEQL_ABORTED; completed scratch stays charged until executing work settles.
Preserve the first execution/cleanup error, including undefined.

tests.nativeR2Case: An actual binding range response is held in the first stage; after cleanup fails, the queued range starts and returns exactly bytes 64–191. All admission and scheduler counters finish at zero.

benchmarks.scope: Same-runtime scheduler-only comparison with current dependencies. Four warmup and eight measured alternating-order rounds. Serial independent stages with held output until caller release; exact admission and zero final charges checked. No cloud, decode, concurrent throughput or total-heap claim.
benchmarks.tradeoff: Mixed timings: empty stages add about 0.6 microseconds each in this run, while one/eight-buffer cases improve. No universal speedup claim; error cleanup is not optional.
benchmarks.simplification: Removed an unnecessary always-created error-recording closure; failure records allocate only on error.

liveCloud.boundary: 64/128-byte engine range-buffer pools, not MiB Worker limits or automatic scanner scheduling. Real public R2 HTTP 206 payloads, read concurrency and release verified.

validation.build: full bundles/declarations and fixture TypeScript passed
validation.fixtureReproducibility: passed; identical hashes and no Git/LFS fixture diff

remaining: Scheduler integration remains numeric replacement stages and explicit scheduled concat/fixture ranges; broader operator integration is still open.
Whole-runtime headroom and scheduler metadata accounting are not proven by this change.

An opaque input owner must implement its ownership contract. If cancellation pinning fails, the stage signal still aborts but scope ownership remains until callback settlement to avoid premature buffer release.
